intro: Bošáca maps two trees from the same hillside hamlet, Zabudišová, and both are national champions. An heirloom apple variety won Slovakia's Tree of the Year contest in 2017 and placed sixth in Europe; a rare pink-fleshed pear won it in 2015 and placed third. They stand 350 metres apart, on ordinary farmland, planted for their fruit rather than for looking at. No other Slovak village has produced two national tree champions from one small stretch of ground, and both still bear fruit every year.
meta_description: Two Slovak Tree of the Year champions, an heirloom apple and a rare pink pear, growing 350 metres apart in the village of Bošáca.
question_meta: Bošáca's oldest documented tree is the Apple Tree of Zabudišová, roughly 130 years old; a pink pear 350 metres away carries no confirmed age.
question_answer: Bošáca's oldest documented tree is the Apple Tree of Zabudišová, a heirloom variety estimated at roughly 130 years old and Slovakia's 2017 Tree of the Year; the pink pear growing 350 metres away carries no confirmed age and may in fact be older.
question_context: Both trees grow in Zabudišová, a hillside hamlet of the village of Bošáca in western Slovakia, and both are national tree champions. The apple carries the rare local variety Citrónové zimné Zabudišovské, planted an estimated 130 years ago by itinerant fruit-growers who moved through the region, and won Slovakia's Strom roka title in 2017 before placing sixth at the European final in 2018. Its girth was measured at 251 centimetres at the time. The pear, Bošácka ružová, is a locally distinctive pink-fleshed variety that won the same national contest two years earlier, in 2015, then placed third in Europe, an unusually strong result. Its age was widely reported in Slovak news as around 200 years, but those articles cannot currently be verified directly, so this page leaves the figure open rather than repeat an unconfirmed number; local tradition ties it to the area's first settlers, which would make it older than the apple. Both trees stand on open farmland with no gate or ticket, reachable on foot from the Zabudišová lane, roughly 15 minutes by car from Nové Mesto nad Váhom.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree in Bošáca?
faq.a: The Apple Tree of Zabudišová, estimated at roughly 130 years old and Slovakia's 2017 Tree of the Year. A pink pear 350 metres away has no confirmed age and may be older.

faq.q: Are both trees free to visit?
faq.a: Yes. Both stand on open farmland outside Zabudišová with no gate, ticket or permission needed.

faq.q: How do the two trees compare?
faq.a: The apple has a documented age of roughly 130 years; the pear's age is unconfirmed but local tradition ties it to the area's first settlers, and it placed higher in the European final. Neither has been remeasured since its contest year.
Both stand in the Zabudišová locality of Bošáca, in the Nové Mesto nad Váhom district, roughly 15 minutes by car from the nearest town. There is no public transport stop at the trees themselves.

trees.name: The Apple Tree of Zabudišová

location.address: roadside in the Zabudišová locality, Bošáca, Nové Mesto nad Váhom District

trees.story:
In 2017 a nearly forgotten apple variety beat every other tree in Slovakia to become that year's national Tree of the Year, then went on to place sixth in the European final the following spring.

Nobody had paid the tree much attention before the contest. It grows on a roadside in Zabudišová, a scattered hamlet of the village of Bošáca, and belongs to Citrónové zimné Zabudišovské, a lemon-yellow winter apple bred locally and grown almost nowhere else. Itinerant fruit-growers, tradesmen who planted orchards for a living and moved on, are thought to have put it in the ground roughly 130 years ago. When it won, it measured two and a half metres round and stood thirteen metres tall, dimensions that make sense for an apple tree left alone for well over a century.

It still fruits. The variety's practical value, a fruit that keeps through winter without a cellar, is presumably why somebody planted it here in the first place, long before there was a competition to win.

Three hundred and fifty metres away, on the same hillside, stands another Slovak Tree of the Year: a pink-fleshed pear that won two years earlier. Two national champions from one small stretch of Zabudišová, which almost nobody outside Bošáca seems to know.
trees.access: Free, roadside tree on a public lane in the Zabudišová part of the village; no gate or permission needed.

trees.name: The Pink Pear of Zabudišová

location.address: near the Zabudišová locality, Bošáca, Nové Mesto nad Váhom District

trees.story:
Slovakia's national tree contest has been won only once by a pear, and this pink-fleshed local variety is it.

Bošácka ružová grows almost nowhere outside this stretch of the Bošáca countryside: a pear whose flesh runs pink rather than white, a curiosity local orchardists have kept going for generations. In 2015 it won the national Strom roka title, then went to the European final and placed third, an unusually strong result for a tree nobody outside its own region had heard of a year earlier.

Local tradition holds that it was planted by the area's first settlers, though nothing pins that to a date. Slovak news coverage after its 2015 win reported a specific age of around two hundred years, a girth of 231 centimetres and a height of 14 metres, but those articles are no longer reachable to check directly, so this page leaves the age open rather than repeat a number it cannot verify itself. What is confirmed, from the region's own tourism writing, is a solitary tree on open land near Zabudišová, unfenced and reachable without asking anyone.

It stands 350 metres from another national champion, an heirloom apple that won two years later. Two prize-winning fruit trees, in one small corner of western Slovakia, planted for eating rather than for looking at. If you know its age, tell us.
trees.access: Free, a solitary tree on open agricultural/village land near Zabudišová; described as reachable, no gate mentioned.
